# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

────────────────────── BEGIN PROMPT ──────────────────────
Claude wrote this prompt. Examine it for inconsistencies against what you
actually find — do not follow it blindly. If a read contradicts a claim here,
trust the read and say so.

You are cleaning up Claudinite's task-label vocabulary across the whole fleet.
You need GitHub issue read+write on every member repo, not just the canon —
if you cannot reach them, stop at step 1 and say which read failed. Never read a
partial or rate-limited sweep as a clean fleet.

The canon repo is missingbulb/Claudinite. The fleet's 14 active members, as
enumerated from missingbulb/Shepherd's usage-fleet.GENERATED.json on 2026-08-24:
ClaudiniteCanary, ClaudiniteWebsite, CrosswordChat, EdFringeNow,
GoogleCalendarEventCreator, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd,
ShoutsAndWhispers, TLDR, VascularColoring, WIP, hitbut, and Claudinite itself.
Re-derive that list rather than trusting it; HelloWorldFlutterApp and gRatio are
dormant and carry no mount.

STEP 1 — unstick the migration. Read missingbulb/Claudinite#1154 and run its
playbook's one remaining leg: across every member, is there an open
[claudinite-work] item parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z whose comments name a
label, a status, or a missing label as the cause? Report per member, from the
issues themselves. If that leg passes, do exactly what #1154 step 4 says:
confirm PR #1152 is open, based on main, green and mergeable, then squash-merge
it with the title "Write the canonical spellings (#1152)". Comment the reads on
#1154 and #1119, then close #1154 completed. If it fails, comment what you read
and leave it open — do not merge.

STEP 2 — wait for the flip to field. #1152 makes the engine write canonical
spellings. Do not relabel anything until every member's stamp
(.claudinite-settings.json, packVersions) shows a claudinite-tasks version at or
above the one #1152 lands, read from each repo's own tracked file. A member
still running the old vendored engine will keep writing legacy spellings, so
relabelling it early just re-dirties.

STEP 3 — relabel CLOSED issues only, in every repo. Open items are NOT touched:
the executor and the scheduler run both mutate an open item's status labels, and
a relabel landing mid-transition is the torn state the janitor escalates. Open
items drain under the decode map on their own. For each closed issue carrying a
legacy spelling, add the canonical label then remove the legacy one — granular
adds and deletes by name, never a set-write (PUT), which clobbers concurrent
transitions. The engine's own ensure pass has already created every canonical
label, so you should not need to create any; if a canonical label is missing in a
repo, create it with the colour and description from QUEUE_LABELS in
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/work-item.mjs rather than inventing one.

  task:blocked      → task:status:blocked
  task:ready        → task:status:waiting-for-executor
  task:executing    → task:status:running-executor
  task:agent        → task:status:running-agent
  task:done         → task:status:done
  outcome:done      → task:status:done
  task:obsolete     → task:status:rejected
  outcome:obsolete  → task:status:rejected
  needs-human + task:needs-human-<kind> → task:status:needs-human-<kind>
      (an issue wearing only bare needs-human takes -failure, the conservative
       lane; where both a bare and a sub-label are present, the sub-label wins)

  DO NOT relabel outcome:delivered. It has no canonical equivalent — the
  approval park replaced it — and outcomeOf still decodes it to the word
  'delivered'. Leave the label and its carriers exactly as they are.

STEP 4 — delete definitions, and only where nothing carries them. For each label
below, count the issues carrying it in that repo (open AND closed, PRs included).
Delete the definition only at a count of zero; at any other count, report the
carriers and leave it. Deleting a label strips it from every issue that has it,
so a nonzero count means data loss, not untidiness.

  Delete when empty: task:blocked, task:ready, task:executing, task:agent,
    task:done, task:obsolete, outcome:done, outcome:obsolete, needs-human,
    task:needs-human-action, task:needs-human-decision,
    task:needs-human-approval, task:needs-human-failure, origin:schedule,
    claude-model:opus, claude-model:sonnet, claude-model:haiku, claude-automerge
  Never delete: outcome:delivered, task:urgent, workflow-failure, claude-task,
    claude-queued, claude-in-review, fleet-adoption, fleet-drift, add-packs,
    task:origin:*, task:status:*
  Leave alone but COUNT and report: ready-for-agent, ready-for-agent-fleet,
    agent-running — see step 5.

STEP 5 — two reads other issues are waiting on. Report both, per member:
  (a) For #1382: does any member carry an open issue titled [claudinite-task]
      (the deleted slot scheduler's dispatch issues)? A zero answer fleet-wide is
      what lets that issue's removal proceed.
  (b) For #1119's tail: does any OPEN work item anywhere still wear a legacy
      status spelling? A zero answer is what lets the decode map's legacy
      entries leave the engine.

STEP 6 — report. One comment on #1119 with a per-member table: what you
relabelled, what you deleted, what you left and why, plus the two step-5 answers.
Comment the step-5 answers on #1382 as well. Do not edit #1119's body — it is
append-only. Do not close #1119; its tail is still open.

Throughout: if a repo refuses a read or a write, say which repo, which call and
what it returned. A repo you could not reach is not a clean repo.
─────────────────────── END PROMPT ───────────────────────

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. ## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

{"number":1152,"title":"Label scheme PR 3: write the canonical spellings","body":"Stage 3 of #1119's plan — the write-side flip. #1138 has landed, so this is rebased onto `main` and its one commit is only the flip.

> ⚠️ **Do not merge before the gate.** The plan gates this on execution step 1: the fleet actually carrying #1138 — every member's executor workflow at HEAD triggering on both ready spellings, judged from each repo's own file. Until then a member that has not taken the new stub stops seeing label events the moment the engine writes the canonical ready spelling — latency, not lost work (the hourly scheduler dispatch is the guaranteed delivery), but the plan's ordering exists to avoid even that.
>
> **#1154 is that gate, and it merges this PR itself.** It is a deferred request on the queue: it reads Shepherd's stamp and workflow file, sweeps every member it can enumerate, and merges this only when all of it passes — re-arming daily until then, and parking for a human if it cannot make the reads.

## What flips

- **The constants every writer already uses now hold today's spellings** — statuses, terminals, and the origin. One edit moves every write site: the generator's occurrence wears `task:origin:planned`, a hand-created item `task:origin:ad-hoc`, a marked issue the same, and the stubs' failure issues `task:origin:github` (that one landed in #1138). Their **names** survive because fielded pack versions import them: a pack still on the old engine writes a legacy label, which every decoder reads as what it always meant.
- **A park stops being a pair.** `needs-human` + a sub-label could be half-applied — a torn state of its own — so a park is one `task:status:needs-human-`, written by one swap. Executor, session converge, scheduler reclaim and the janitor's sweep all follow.
- **The legacy spellings become explicit `LEGACY_*` literals.** The decode map was built from the constants that just moved; left alone it would have mapped today's spelling to itself and forgotten the vocabulary it exists to read. They stay in the ensure-list too — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue that carries it.
- **The dashboard follows** with its own display key for the park column, rather than borrowing a label nothing writes.
- **The re-queue lever is one exported phrase**: clearing the status *is* the re-ask, so the five messages that said "remove the `needs-human` labels" now say that, from one home.
- **Writer-facing prose swept**: the session instructions' park table, the request worker's brief, and `writing-tasks`.

## Folders touched

```
engine/scheduler/queue/       the write constants, the one-label park, origins on
                              every born item, the shared re-queue phrase, and the
                              session/worker briefs that tell an agent what to write
packs/basics/                 the janitor's sweep writes one park label; version bumped
packs/claudinite-dashboard/   the park column gets its own display key; version bumped
packs/claudinite-growth/      writing-tasks states today's vocabulary; version bumped
```

Note on versions: `basics` and `claudinite-dashboard` are bumped **again** here (`.2`). They already moved in #1138, and `pack-version-bumped` compares against `main` — so it could not see that these edits ride a version #1138 has already delivered. Without the second bump they would reach nobody.

## Verification

Re-run after the rebase onto the squashed `main`: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2409 pass, 0 fail; `check_the_work` clean.

`vocabulary.test.mjs` gains the write side: every write constant is a canonical status, a park is one label, a kind word resolves to it, and the re-queue phrase names clearing the status. Seen to fail with the flip reverted. The 43 test failures the flip caused were all write-assertion churn — updated in place, and the legacy-spelling coverage now lives where it belongs, in the decode tests.

{"number":1382,"title":"Retire the deleted slot scheduler's leftovers — its labels, its session-side resolver, its janitor rules","body":"The slot scheduler is gone: `repo-context.mjs` now rejects `taskScheduler.dispatch: "slots"` outright ("the work-item queue is the only dispatch mechanism; `"slots"` named the slot scheduler, which is deleted"). Its surface did not go with it, and it is still ensured, still read, and still capable of acting on issues.

**The labels** (`dispatch.mjs`'s `SCHEDULER_LABELS`): `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-agent-fleet`, `agent-running`, `needs-human`, `workflow-failure`. The task-janitor ensures all five on every run that finds a leftover `[claudinite-task]` dispatch issue, and *re-applies* a ready label to one it judges un-triggered (`rearmDispatchIssues`) or escalates it to `needs-human` (`staleClaimedDispatchIssues`). `workflow-failure` is the one string that must survive — `queue/workflow-failure.mjs` writes it for real — and it is defined twice, once in each module.

**The session side**: `resolve-dispatch.mjs` (its whole reason for existing is resolving which `ready-for-agent`-labelled dispatch a session was woken for), `validate-dispatch.mjs`, and `executor.md`. The queue never arms a label event — `queue/invoke.mjs` fires a routine with a nonce and the session reads `queue/instructions.md` — so none of that participates in a live hand-off.

**What gates the removal**: whether any member still carries an open `[claudinite-task]` issue. While one exists, deleting the janitor's two rules abandons it, and deleting the labels strips them off it. That is a fleet-wide issue read this repo cannot make, so it belongs to the same cleanup pass as #1119's label sweep; the answer it needs is one line per member.

**Overlaps** #1341 (eliminate the task-janitor: fold its recovery into the scheduler run) — if that lands first, the two dispatch rules are deleted rather than moved, and this issue is only the labels, the resolver and `executor.md`.

{"number":1152,"title":"Label scheme PR 3: write the canonical spellings","body":"Stage 3 of #1119's plan — the write-side flip. #1138 has landed, so this is rebased onto `main` and its one commit is only the flip.

> ⚠️ **Do not merge before the gate.** The plan gates this on execution step 1: the fleet actually carrying #1138 — every member's executor workflow at HEAD triggering on both ready spellings, judged from each repo's own file. Until then a member that has not taken the new stub stops seeing label events the moment the engine writes the canonical ready spelling — latency, not lost work (the hourly scheduler dispatch is the guaranteed delivery), but the plan's ordering exists to avoid even that.
>
> **#1154 is that gate, and it merges this PR itself.** It is a deferred request on the queue: it reads Shepherd's stamp and workflow file, sweeps every member it can enumerate, and merges this only when all of it passes — re-arming daily until then, and parking for a human if it cannot make the reads.

## What flips

- **The constants every writer already uses now hold today's spellings** — statuses, terminals, and the origin. One edit moves every write site: the generator's occurrence wears `task:origin:planned`, a hand-created item `task:origin:ad-hoc`, a marked issue the same, and the stubs' failure issues `task:origin:github` (that one landed in #1138). Their **names** survive because fielded pack versions import them: a pack still on the old engine writes a legacy label, which every decoder reads as what it always meant.
- **A park stops being a pair.** `needs-human` + a sub-label could be half-applied — a torn state of its own — so a park is one `task:status:needs-human-`, written by one swap. Executor, session converge, scheduler reclaim and the janitor's sweep all follow.
- **The legacy spellings become explicit `LEGACY_*` literals.** The decode map was built from the constants that just moved; left alone it would have mapped today's spelling to itself and forgotten the vocabulary it exists to read. They stay in the ensure-list too — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue that carries it.
- **The dashboard follows** with its own display key for the park column, rather than borrowing a label nothing writes.
- **The re-queue lever is one exported phrase**: clearing the status *is* the re-ask, so the five messages that said "remove the `needs-human` labels" now say that, from one home.
- **Writer-facing prose swept**: the session instructions' park table, the request worker's brief, and `writing-tasks`.

## Folders touched

```
engine/scheduler/queue/       the write constants, the one-label park, origins on
                              every born item, the shared re-queue phrase, and the
                              session/worker briefs that tell an agent what to write
packs/basics/                 the janitor's sweep writes one park label; version bumped
packs/claudinite-dashboard/   the park column gets its own display key; version bumped
packs/claudinite-growth/      writing-tasks states today's vocabulary; version bumped
```

Note on versions: `basics` and `claudinite-dashboard` are bumped **again** here (`.2`). They already moved in #1138, and `pack-version-bumped` compares against `main` — so it could not see that these edits ride a version #1138 has already delivered. Without the second bump they would reach nobody.

## Verification

Re-run after the rebase onto the squashed `main`: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2409 pass, 0 fail; `check_the_work` clean.

`vocabulary.test.mjs` gains the write side: every write constant is a canonical status, a park is one label, a kind word resolves to it, and the re-queue phrase names clearing the status. Seen to fail with the flip reverted. The 43 test failures the flip caused were all write-assertion churn — updated in place, and the legacy-spelling coverage now lives where it belongs, in the decode tests.

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. input.body:
Stage 3 of #1119 — the write-side flip. **Supersedes #1152**, which cannot merge: `mergeable_state: "dirty"`, 11 content conflicts, and its whole diff was written against `engine/scheduler/queue/`, a directory #1317 has since moved to `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/`. Its green also predates 52 commits on `main`.

The gate #1152 waited on is satisfied. #1154's `Verify:` now passes on all three legs — the two file legs were confirmed fleet-wide on 2026-08-24, and the third (no member parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z citing a label, a status or a missing label) was read this session across all 14 active members. The parks are `converge-item.mjs` auth failures, a missing `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, a `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT` and one 404 — none of them the label scheme. Full reads: #1119.

## What flips

- **The write constants hold today's spellings** — statuses, terminals, and the origin on every born item. Their *names* survive because fielded pack versions import them: a pack still on the old engine writes a legacy label, which every decoder reads as what it always meant.
- **A park stops being a pair.** `needs-human` + a sub-label could be half-applied — a torn state of its own — so a park is one `task:status:needs-human-<kind>`, written by one swap. Executor, session converge, scheduler reclaim and the janitor's sweep all follow.
- **The legacy spellings become explicit `LEGACY_*` literals.** The decode map was built from the constants that just moved; left alone it would have mapped today's spelling to itself and forgotten the vocabulary it exists to read. They stay in `QUEUE_LABELS` — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue carrying it.
- **The dashboard gets its own `PARKED` display key** rather than borrowing a label nothing writes.
- **The re-queue lever is one exported phrase** — clearing the status *is* the re-ask.
- **Writer-facing prose swept**: the session instructions' park table, the request worker's brief, and `writing-tasks`.

## What this re-land adds over #1152

`packs/claudinite-dashboard/work.mjs` and `next-work.mjs` did not exist when the flip was first written. Both used `NEEDS_HUMAN` as a **state key** exactly as `fleet.mjs` and `ui.mjs` did, so a straight rebase would have left them comparing `stateOf()`'s output against a label the engine no longer writes — no error, no failing test, just **zero parked items counted on both dashboards**. They are converted to `PARKED` with the rest. `model.mjs` also stops re-exporting the now-deprecated `NEEDS_HUMAN`, so the same mistake cannot be made again from the page side.

The scheduler's reclaim also drops its separate `op.triage` write — with a one-label park, nothing produces `op.triage` any more, and the line was a dead read.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/     the write constants and the LEGACY_* literals, the
                            one-label park, origins on every born item, the shared
                            re-queue phrase, and the session/worker briefs that tell
                            an agent what to write. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-dashboard/ the parked state becomes the page's own PARKED key across
                            all five modules that read it. Version bumped.
packs/basics/               the janitor's sweep writes one park label. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-growth/    writing-tasks states today's vocabulary. Version bumped.
```

## Verification

Run against **current `main`**, not the branch's own base:

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **2745 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_work` — **0 blocking, 0 advisory**.
- `check_the_world` — **0 blocking, 88 advisory**, byte-identical to the same command run on `origin/main` in a clean worktree. No finding is introduced by this change.

The four failures the flip caused were all write-assertion churn (`task:done` → `task:status:done`, `task:ready` → `task:status:waiting-for-executor`, and a born item now wearing its origin), fixed in place. `vocabulary.test.mjs` carries the write side: every write constant is a canonical status, a park is one label, a kind word resolves to it, and the re-queue phrase names clearing the status.

## What this does NOT do

It does not relabel anything, and it deletes no label definition. Both are #1119's tail and both are still blocked — the relabel on this landing plus a fleet converge, and the deletions on `QUEUE_LABELS` dropping the legacy names, which cannot happen while ~176 open items fleet-wide still wear them. See #1119 for the per-member picture.

Refs #1119

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

content.content:
---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

{"number":1385,"title":"Label scheme PR 3, re-landed: write the canonical spellings","body":"Stage 3 of #1119 — the write-side flip. **Supersedes #1152**, which cannot merge: `mergeable_state: "dirty"`, 11 content conflicts, and its whole diff was written against `engine/scheduler/queue/`, a directory #1317 has since moved to `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/`. Its green also predates 52 commits on `main`.

The gate #1152 waited on is satisfied. #1154's `Verify:` now passes on all three legs — the two file legs were confirmed fleet-wide on 2026-08-24, and the third (no member parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z citing a label, a status or a missing label) was read this session across all 14 active members. The parks are `converge-item.mjs` auth failures, a missing `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, a `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT` and one 404 — none of them the label scheme. Full reads: #1119.

## What flips

- **The write constants hold today's spellings** — statuses, terminals, and the origin on every born item. Their *names* survive because fielded pack versions import them: a pack still on the old engine writes a legacy label, which every decoder reads as what it always meant.
- **A park stops being a pair.** `needs-human` + a sub-label could be half-applied — a torn state of its own — so a park is one `task:status:needs-human-`, written by one swap. Executor, session converge, scheduler reclaim and the janitor's sweep all follow.
- **The legacy spellings become explicit `LEGACY_*` literals.** The decode map was built from the constants that just moved; left alone it would have mapped today's spelling to itself and forgotten the vocabulary it exists to read. They stay in `QUEUE_LABELS` — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue carrying it.
- **The dashboard gets its own `PARKED` display key** rather than borrowing a label nothing writes.
- **The re-queue lever is one exported phrase** — clearing the status *is* the re-ask.
- **Writer-facing prose swept**: the session instructions' park table, the request worker's brief, and `writing-tasks`.

## What this re-land adds over #1152

`packs/claudinite-dashboard/work.mjs` and `next-work.mjs` did not exist when the flip was first written. Both used `NEEDS_HUMAN` as a **state key** exactly as `fleet.mjs` and `ui.mjs` did, so a straight rebase would have left them comparing `stateOf()`'s output against a label the engine no longer writes — no error, no failing test, just **zero parked items counted on both dashboards**. They are converted to `PARKED` with the rest. `model.mjs` also stops re-exporting the now-deprecated `NEEDS_HUMAN`, so the same mistake cannot be made again from the page side.

The scheduler's reclaim also drops its separate `op.triage` write — with a one-label park, nothing produces `op.triage` any more, and the line was a dead read.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/     the write constants and the LEGACY_* literals, the
                            one-label park, origins on every born item, the shared
                            re-queue phrase, and the session/worker briefs that tell
                            an agent what to write. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-dashboard/ the parked state becomes the page's own PARKED key across
                            all five modules that read it. Version bumped.
packs/basics/               the janitor's sweep writes one park label. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-growth/    writing-tasks states today's vocabulary. Version bumped.
```

## Verification

Run against **current `main`**, not the branch's own base:

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **2745 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_work` — **0 blocking, 0 advisory**.
- `check_the_world` — **0 blocking, 88 advisory**, byte-identical to the same command run on `origin/main` in a clean worktree. No finding is introduced by this change.

The four failures the flip caused were all write-assertion churn (`task:done` → `task:status:done`, `task:ready` → `task:status:waiting-for-executor`, and a born item now wearing its origin), fixed in place. `vocabulary.test.mjs` carries the write side: every write constant is a canonical status, a park is one label, a kind word resolves to it, and the re-queue phrase names clearing the status.

## What this does NOT do

It does not relabel anything, and it deletes no label definition. Both are #1119's tail and both are still blocked — the relabel on this landing plus a fleet converge, and the deletions on `QUEUE_LABELS` dropping the legacy names, which cannot happen while ~176 open items fleet-wide still wear them. See #1119 for the per-member picture.

Refs #1119
